name: Resilient Orders Sync
desc:
You are writing the extraction step that copies orders from an unreliable partner API. Pages are numbered from 1. The API sometimes fails, and because orders are updated while you paginate, the same order can appear on several pages with different versions.

The environment provides:

class ApiError(Exception):
    """Raised by fetch_page when the API answers with an HTTP error."""
    def __init__(self, status: int, retry_after: Optional[float] = None):
        self.status = status            # HTTP status code, e.g. 404, 429, 503
        self.retry_after = retry_after  # seconds to wait, sometimes sent with a 429; may be None

def fetch_page(page: int) -> dict:
    """Returns {"items": [...], "next_page": int or None}.
    May raise ApiError or the built-in TimeoutError."""

def sleep(seconds: float) -> None:
    """Waits the given number of seconds. Use it instead of time.sleep."""

Each item is a dict with at least an id (int) and an updated_at (ISO 8601 string with a UTC offset, e.g. "2024-05-01T10:00:00+02:00"), plus other fields.

Rules

  1. Start with page 1 and follow next_page until it is None.
  2. Retryable errors are: TimeoutError, and ApiError with status 429 or with a status between 500 and 599 (inclusive). Any other ApiError (for example 400, 401, 404) must be raised immediately, without retry and without sleeping.
  3. Each page is requested at most max_attempts times in total (first call included). The attempt counter starts again from 1 for every page. If all attempts fail, raise the exception of the last attempt, unchanged.
  4. Before the k-th retry of a page (k = 1, 2, 3, ...), call sleep(delay) exactly once, where delay = 2 ** (k - 1) (1, 2, 4, ...). Exception: if the error that triggered the retry is an ApiError with status 429 and a retry_after that is not None, use delay = retry_after. Never sleep after the last attempt, never call time.sleep.
  5. Deduplicate the items by id: keep the version with the latest updated_at, comparing actual instants (offsets matter). If two versions have the same instant, keep the one received last.
  6. Return the kept items, unchanged (same dicts), sorted by id ascending.

Example

Successive outcomes of fetch_page:

call outcome
fetch_page(1) raises TimeoutError
fetch_page(1) returns {"items": [{"id": 2, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T09:00:00+00:00", "v": "b1"}, {"id": 1, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T10:00:00+00:00", "v": "a1"}], "next_page": 2}
fetch_page(2) raises ApiError(503)
fetch_page(2) raises ApiError(429, retry_after=7)
fetch_page(2) returns {"items": [{"id": 1, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T11:00:00+00:00", "v": "a2"}, {"id": 3, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T08:00:00+00:00", "v": "c1"}], "next_page": None}

Expected calls to sleep: sleep(1), sleep(1), sleep(7).

Expected return value:

[
    {"id": 1, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T11:00:00+00:00", "v": "a2"},
    {"id": 2, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T09:00:00+00:00", "v": "b1"},
    {"id": 3, "updated_at": "2024-05-01T08:00:00+00:00", "v": "c1"},
]

Function signature

def sync_orders(fetch_page, sleep, max_attempts: int = 4) -> list:
    ...

Constraints

  • Python 3 standard library only (datetime and json are available). ApiError is already defined: do not redefine it.
  • Up to 10^4 pages, up to 500 items per page.

The functions described in the task (the API) are provided by the tests: you only write your function.

[execution time limit] 4 seconds (py3)
[memory limit] 1 GB
